proof.log_convexity: u_s*u_(1-s)>=u_(1/2)^2=gamma^2 by log-convexity of a sum of exponentials, including q=1 by a one-sided limit
proof.spectral_lower_bound: T_ij=w_j unless j reverses i, w=(u,u,v,v). T is similar to symmetric S_ij=sqrt(w_i*w_j) on allowed transitions. The Rayleigh quotient of sqrt(w) is 2*(u^2+u*v+v^2)/(u+v)=2*((u+v)-u*v/(u+v))>=3*sqrt(u*v).
proof.sharpness: At s=1/2, u=v=gamma=sqrt(p*(1-p))*(sqrt(q)+sqrt(1-q)); every T row sums to 3*gamma, so inf_(0<s<1) rho(T)=3*gamma.
proof.p_0_30_conclusion: For q in [1/2,1], 3*gamma>=3*sqrt(0.3*0.7)=1.37477270848675>1. No fixed global Chernoff exponent makes this nonbacktracking path sum summable at p=.30.

numerical_check: Positive-matrix power iteration to 1e-15 relative vector tolerance; independently checked all 12 cells by numpy.linalg.eigvals, with maximum absolute discrepancy 4.42e-13 against the rounded stored values. The s=1/2 row-sum bound and s<->1-s symmetry agree.
scope: Only the pathwise Markov/Chernoff bound with one global exponent and unrestricted nonbacktracking path enumeration is ruled out. This does not bound true H12 at p=.30, exclude self-avoiding or path-dependent estimates, or locate a phase boundary.
